chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad — all of them from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Salih al-Nayli who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Do the servants have any capability?' He said, then he said to me: 'When they perform the deed, they are capable — with the capability that God has placed within them.' He said, I said: 'And what is it?' He said: 'The instrument. For example, an adulterer — when he commits adultery, he was capable of the adultery at the time he committed it; and had he abstained from adultery and not committed it, he would have been capable of abstaining when he abstained.'

He said, then he said: 'There is not for him any capability before the deed — neither little nor much — but at the time of the deed and the abstaining, he was capable.' I said: 'Then for what does He punish him?' He said: 'Due to the compelling proof and the instrument He has implanted within them. Indeed, God does not compel anyone to disobey Him, nor does He will with a determined will that anyone disbelieve.

But when he does disbelieve, it was within God's will that he disbelieve; and they are within God's will and within His knowledge that they will not turn toward anything of goodness.' I said: 'Did He will that they disbelieve?' He said: 'I am not saying it like that. Rather, I say: He knew that they would disbelieve, so He willed disbelief due to His knowledge regarding them. But it is not a determined will — rather it is a will of choice.'

key_terms.إرادة اختيار: Will of choice — divine foreknowledge-based will that respects human free will
key_terms.إرادة حتم: Determined/compulsory will — divine decree that forces an outcome without human choice
key_terms.الآلة: Instrument/tool — used here to denote the faculty of capability installed by God in human beings
key_terms.الاستطاعة: Capability/power — the technical term for human ability to act, debated extensively in kalam (Islamic theology)
key_terms.الحجة البالغة: The compelling proof — refers to God's conclusive argument against humanity on Judgment Day

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq teach about human free will and divine capability?
ai.summary: This hadith presents Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq's (AS) nuanced doctrine on human capability (al-istitaa'a) and divine will — a central issue debated between the Mu'tazila (who affirmed pre-action capability) and the Ash'ariyya (who denied human agency). The Imam articulates a middle position: capability is realized concurrently with the action, not prior to it, but God is not a compeller of sin either. God's 'will' regarding disbelief is a will of foreknowledge (iradah ikhtiyar) rather than a determined coercive decree (iradah hatm) — a distinction that preserves both divine omniscience and human moral accountability.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Salih Al Nayli who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is there any capability for the servants for anything?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘When they are doing the deed, so they are being capable with the capability which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Made to be in them’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘And what is it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The tool. For example an adulterer when he commits adultery, he was capable of the adultery when he did commit adultery; and had he neglected the adultery and had not committed adultery, he would have been capable of neglecting it when he did neglect it’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There isn’t for him from the capability before the deed, neither little nor more, but with the deed, and the neglecting, he was capable’. 
I said, ‘So what is that upon which he would be Punished?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Due to the sensible arguments, and the tool which is placed within them. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Does not Compel anyone upon disobeying Him<sup>azwj</sup>, nor does He<sup>azwj</sup> Intend a Determined Intention of the disbelief from anyone, but when he does disbelieve, it would be in the Intention of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that he does disbelieve, and they are in the Intention of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and in His<sup>azwj</sup> Knowledge that they would not be coming to anything from the good’. 
I said, ‘He<sup>azwj</sup> Intends from them that they disbelieve?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It isn’t like this that I<sup>asws</sup> am saying. But, I<sup>asws</sup> am saying that He<sup>azwj</sup> Knows that they would be disbelieving, so the Intention of the disbelief is due to His<sup>azwj</sup> Knowledge regarding them, but it isn’t the Determined Intention. But rather, it is an Intention of choice’.
